web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan
question: Weighing NIKE's North America wholesale inflection against China's -26% contraction, 25.5x forward P/E, and sub-200D tape, what is our exact 3-horizon verdict and capital allocation plan?

epigraph.quote: The best turnaround investments are made not when the CEO announces a plan, nor when the stock is cheapest on hope, but when fundamentals stop bleeding and the price confirms the turn.
epigraph.author: Institutional Turnaround Playbook

web_blocks.title: Quarterly Verification Milestones & Thesis Invalidation Triggers

web_blocks.html: Upgrade / Entry Triggers & Invalidation Stop: Upgrade NKE from `TIER_3` Watchlist only if (1) price pulls back into $33.50–$35.00 with volume support AND Dec 17 Q2 FY2027 filings confirm gross margin >= 43.5% ex-tariff recoveries with Greater China moderating from -26% CC (2.43:1 R:R to $43.50 vs. $31.50 stop), OR (2) weekly close reclaims > $40.77 on >= 1.5x volume with China stabilizing. A daily/weekly close below $31.50 triggers an immediate exit of all 74.5773 Robinhood shares [2, 3, 24].

Sizing discipline matters as much as entry price. Even if NKE holds the $33.50–$35.00 zone, its `CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL` / `TIER_3` status caps initial sizing at a half-weight starter (or a defined-risk Bull Call Spread capped at ~55 bps of NAV) with a hard $31.50 stop [29]. Full core sizing waits for confirmed Stage 2 recovery and FCF exceeding the $2.41B dividend [2].

Why not average in slowly at $37.99 if you like the long-term brand? Averaging into a falling 200-day moving average ties up opportunity cost and violates asymmetric risk rules. At $37.99, you risk $6.49 to the $31.50 stop to make $5.51 to our $43.50 base target (0.85:1). Waiting for $33.50–$35.00 flips that exact math to 2.43:1 [29]. Price discipline is the entire edge.

Finally, this dossier's pipeline sync keeps NKE on the US Watchlist as a `COMPLETED` `TIER_3` name rather than promoting it to the active Shortlist. It will remain on watch until December 17 Q2 FY2027 results and weekly price action resolve the tension between North America wholesale recovery and Greater China contraction [3, 24, 29].

Our options desk audit reaches the exact same conclusion. With 30-day ATM implied volatility at 44.3% versus 35.0% realized volatility (`IV_ELEVATED`), buying outright calls at $37.99 destroys edge [29]. Only a successful test of the $34.02 shelf justifies deploying a defined-risk January 2027 $37.5/$42.5 Bull Call Debit Spread ($1.82 debit, $546 max loss, $954 max profit) [29]. Until then, cash remains the highest-conviction position.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the desk decision. You and I have walked through Phil Knight's sixty-year history, every geographic segment, the Vietnam-and-Indonesia factory floor, the $100-to-$4.71 free cash flow waterfall, the competitive assault from On and HOKA, Elliott Hill's 'Win Now' reset, the Reverse DCF at $37.99, and the weekly price chart. Now we put it all on one scale and make a clean, unhedged call.

Start with the honest Bull vs. Bear ledger. The Bull is right that NIKE is not Under Armour: it still commands $46.4 billion in annual revenue, holds $9.03 billion in cash against $7.94 billion in debt, and just posted +9% wholesale growth in North America as Dick's Sporting Goods and Foot Locker welcome the Swoosh back onto prime shelves. Plus, CEO Elliott Hill and directors Tim Cook and Robert Swan put real personal cash to work in the open market.

Yet the Bear holds three decisive cards right now. First, Greater China is still in freefall—down 26% in constant currency in Q1 FY2027—while NIKE Direct fell 8% and Converse plunged 28%. Second, FY2026 free cash flow of $2.18 billion did not cover the $2.41 billion dividend, and GAAP operating income was flattered by $986 million in one-time tariff recoveries. Third, at $37.99, you are still paying 25.54x forward earnings—more than double Deckers' 10.69x forward P/E—while the stock sits 15.2% below a falling 200-day moving average in a US market Correction.

Put those probabilities into cold numbers. If we assign 35% odds to a Bear stagnation case ($30.00), 45% odds to a gradual Base wholesale recovery ($43.50), and 20% odds to a full Bull flywheel ($60.00), the probability-weighted expected value is $42.08—barely 10.8% above today's $37.99 close. With an invalidation stop below the $31.97 cycle low at $31.50, buying at $37.99 risks $6.49 to make $5.51 to our base target. That is a 0.85-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. You and I do not take 0.85-to-1 bets.

Therefore, our New-Capital Verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3 Watchlist), and our Current Holding Action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP on our existing 74.5773 shares in Robinhood ($2,850.00 cost basis, $2,833.19 market value, 3.19% portfolio weight). We protect those existing shares with a hard invalidation stop at $31.50, and we set two disciplined alerts for any fresh capital: either a pullback into the $33.50–$35.00 support shelf backed by December 17 Q2 FY2027 confirmation (2.43:1 R:R to $43.50), or a confirmed high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above the 30-week SMA ($40.77) and 200-day SMA ($44.79). Until one of those triggers fires, 100% of our marginal cash stays in T-bills.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good investing is mostly waiting. At $37.99, NKE offers only 0.85:1 reward-to-risk to our $43.50 base target. At $33.50–$35.00, that exact same thesis offers 2.43:1. Patience turns a mediocre bet into an asymmetric one.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash Beats Both NKE and Peers Today
paragraphs: Whenever we pass on a stock at today's price, we owe ourselves an opportunity-cost check: is there a better home for the next $10,000 right now? On our active US Shortlist, BrightSpring Health Services (BTSG) is in a genuine Stage 2 uptrend, but it is already extended 10.8% above its 10-week EMA and needs a pullback to $63.29–$67.76. Outside the shortlist, Deckers Outdoor (DECK) boasts 38.1% ROIC at 10.7x forward earnings, yet it too sits in a Stage 1 consolidation waiting for support at $83.84–$86.90.

With the S&P 500 in a Correction and six distribution days on the tape, holding 100% of marginal capital in USD cash/T-bills is not passivity—it is preserving dry powder for the moment either NKE or a higher-ROIC leader hits an asymmetric entry zone.

book_subsections.title: The December 17 Scorecard: What Changes Our Mind
paragraphs: Finally, let's write down the exact scoreboard for the next two quarters so we never shift the goalposts later. On December 17, 2026, when NIKE reports Q2 FY2027 results, you and I will check three lines first: Greater China constant-currency revenue, gross margin excluding one-time tariff recoveries, and trailing free cash flow relative to the $2.41 billion dividend.

If Greater China narrows its decline from -26% toward single digits, gross margin stabilizes above 44%, and price holds the $33.50–$35.00 shelf or surges back above $40.77 on heavy institutional volume, NIKE earns an immediate re-rating from TIER_3 watch to an active turnaround buy. If instead China stays broken and shares slice below $31.50, our stop rule protects capital and we move on without hesitation.
